prose: Sean Goedecke on two adjacent debates. First, the Anthropic researcher's resignation tweet that revived AI-apocalypse talk - 'the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade' - and the skeptical readings: PR for regulation, self-promotion, stock-pumping, or proof-by-absurdity ('if you believed it you'd be bombing datacenters, not posting').

Second, his title argument: lots of people now say we should stop building software for humans and start building for AI agents. It sort of makes sense - his own agents already use Datadog more than he does, purely by moving faster through more things. The essay pushes back on where that logic ends. (Summary based on the article's opening sections.)
